title: Observe MinIO primary-volume capacity

gates.name: Python typecheck
gates.command: docker compose run --rm --no-deps backend python -m mypy src/face_moment

gates.name: MinIO capacity tests
gates.command: docker compose run --rm backend python -m pytest tests/infrastructure/test_minio_capacity.py

evidence_required: .memory-bank/domains/photo-processing.md#minio-capacity-observation RED: the PostgreSQL probe outcome does not provide an independent MinIO observation; GREEN: disposable normal, low-threshold and unavailable MinIO fixtures return exact current status/bytes/threshold/time/error through one private read-only view while PostgreSQL remains normal; decisive comparison: MinIO changes alone alter only its result, the view rejects writes, forbidden path/object/credential/media markers remain absent and cleanup leaves PostgreSQL untouched; artifact: paired redacted capacity, topology and marker-scan output.
purpose: Add the independent configured read-only MinIO primary-volume observation using the minimal capacity mechanism established for PostgreSQL.
success_outcome: The backend observes MinIO capacity as ok, low or unavailable independently of PostgreSQL while the volume, objects and internal service stay private and read-only.
anti_goals: Do not couple MinIO status to PostgreSQL, expose paths/object keys/media/credentials or add another probe framework.
Do not add history, alerts, product capacity targets, public MinIO routes or write access to the volume view.

forbidden_scope: Realtime reference-query execution and participant result assembly owned by FT-004
Calibration calculation, recommendation and run persistence owned by FT-011
Photo delete, restore and hard-purge behavior owned by FT-012
stop_conditions: MinIO cannot use its own configured read-only view and the same minimal statvfs-equivalent mechanism.
Proof would require production objects, public storage access, Docker API or another monitoring service.

constraints: Reuse the minimal capacity value/adapter from TASK-033; add only independent MinIO configuration and observation.
Use disposable Compose resources and synthetic object/path markers with safe rerun and owner-bounded cleanup.
Keep PostgreSQL normal while exercising each MinIO branch to prove independence.
invariants: MinIO remains private and the backend capacity view is read-only.
One store's failure never erases or reuses the other store's current result.
No path, object key, commercial media or credential enters output or logs.
verification_targets: Disposable proof covers normal, configured-low and unavailable MinIO with PostgreSQL kept normal, read-only/private topology, marker redaction and cleanup.
